content: Self-preference bias in LLM-as-judge (arXiv 2410.21819 and follow-ups): judges score lower-perplexity text higher, and their own outputs are necessarily lower perplexity, so models systematically favour their own and same-family outputs. Sycophancy compounds it: assertive claims get rated higher even when wrong. Self-Attribution Bias (arXiv 2603.04582) shows AI monitors go easy on themselves. Models show a self-correction blind spot: they fix errors from external sources but not identical errors in their own output. Implication for reviewer/tester agents: never use the same model instance/session as the developer, cross-family review reduces rubber-stamping.
